## formal
Let $L_{N} = \Cl(N, N{+}2)$ be a tower level, written as the anisotropic kernel $\mathrm{span}\{g_{1}, g_{2}\}$ ($Q = -1, -1$) orthogonal to $N$ hyperbolic planes $(e_{j}, f_{j})$, $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, with $v_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j}) = a_{j}^{*}$, $w_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} - f_{j}) = a_{j}$ (the canonical anticommutation relations, Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}), $n_{j} = v_{j}w_{j}$, $\omega_{j} = e_{j}f_{j}$, $\Gamma = \prod_{j}\omega_{j}$, $J = g_{1}g_{2}$, and $*$ the adjoint (reversion composed with the sign flip of the generators of square $-1$). A \emph{spin assignment} is $s = (s_{1}, \dots, s_{N})$ with $s_{j} \in \tfrac12\mathbb{Z}$, the weights of a rotation of the one-particle space that is diagonal in the mode basis; it defines $L_{s} = \sum_{j}s_{j}n_{j}$ and
\[
U_{s}(\theta) = e^{\theta JL_{s}} = \prod_{j}\bigl(1 - n_{j} + n_{j}e^{\theta Js_{j}}\bigr), \qquad e^{\varphi J} = \cos\varphi + J\sin\varphi .
\]
An element $x$ has \emph{integer} (\emph{half-integer}) \emph{spin} if $U_{s}(2\pi)\,x\,U_{s}(2\pi)^{*} = x$ ($= -x$). Two elements obey Bose (Fermi) statistics if they commute (anticommute).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The turn by $2\pi$.)} $J^{2} = -1$, $J^{*} = -J$, and $J$ commutes with every plane generator. $U_{s}(\theta)$ is unitary, commutes with $J$, satisfies $U_{s}(\theta)U_{s}(\theta') = U_{s}(\theta + \theta')$, and $U_{s}(\theta)w_{j}U_{s}(\theta)^{*} = e^{-\theta Js_{j}}w_{j}$, $U_{s}(\theta)v_{j}U_{s}(\theta)^{*} = e^{\theta Js_{j}}v_{j}$. Since $n_{j} = \tfrac12(1 - \omega_{j})$,
\[
U_{s}(2\pi) = \prod_{j:\ s_{j} \in \mathbb{Z} + \frac12}\omega_{j} ,
\]
the product of the volume elements of the planes of half-integer weight.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Spin and statistics agree exactly when every mode is a spinor.)} $\operatorname{Ad}U_{s}(2\pi) = \operatorname{Ad}\Gamma$ on the algebra of the planes if and only if every $s_{j}$ is half-integer, and then $U_{s}(2\pi) = \Gamma$. In that case an element of definite spin has half-integer spin exactly when it is odd, two odd elements on disjoint sets of modes anticommute and every other pair on disjoint sets commutes; in particular every hopping element $v_{i}w_{j}$, pairing element $w_{i}w_{j}$, collective sum of them and density mode $\rho_{q} = \sum_{k}v_{k}w_{k+q}$ has integer spin and Bose statistics across blocks, exactly at every $N$, with no limit taken.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Counter-model: a boson of half-integer spin.)} Let some $s_{j}$ be an integer. Then $w_{j}$ has integer spin and anticommutes with every other mode. Take $N_{b}$ blocks, the lower mode of each with weight $\tfrac12$ and the upper with weight $0$, and $b_{i} = v_{\mathrm{lower},i}w_{\mathrm{upper},i}$. Each $b_{i}$ has half-integer spin; the $b_{i}$ and $b_{i}^{*}$ of distinct blocks commute; and $B = N_{b}^{-1/2}\sum_{i}b_{i}$ is the hopping ladder of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(ii): on $(B^{*})^{k}P_{\mathrm{pol}}$, $[B, B^{*}] = 1 - 2k/N_{b}$, $k = 0, \dots, N_{b}$, so $B$ tends on states of bounded $k$ to a canonical boson mode of half-integer spin.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The level's own rotations give integer spin.)} $\operatorname{Ad}e^{\varphi J}$ fixes every element of the algebra of the planes, for every $\varphi$. The real rotation of two modes, $L = v_{0}w_{1} - v_{1}w_{0} = \tfrac12(e_{0}e_{1} - f_{0}f_{1})$, is a sum of two commuting bivectors of square $-1$; $[L, w_{0} \pm Jw_{1}] = \pm J(w_{0} \pm Jw_{1})$, so its weights are $\pm1$; $e^{\pi L} = \omega_{0}\omega_{1}$ negates both modes and $e^{2\pi L} = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (i) to (iv) are proved. \emph{Reading.} On the ladder, statistics is the grading of the algebra and holds exactly at every $N$; spin is the extra datum $s$. Spin and statistics agree for the collective modes if and only if they agree for the single modes, so the collective limit neither produces nor repairs the connection: half-integer spin with anticommutation and integer spin with commutation for the bosons is equivalent to every tower mode being a spinor. The tower does not fix that datum: by (iv) the rotations it supplies by itself give integer spin to everything, and half-integer weights need the kernel unit $J$ at half angle. For the attached free fields the spinor assignment of the CAR modes is supplied by locality with a positive norm (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}), a continuum input.

## technical
On the tower, fermion modes anticommute and products of two modes on distinct blocks commute: this is the grading of the algebra and holds exactly for any number of modes. Spin is a separate datum: how a rotation acts on each mode. With the kernel bivector $J$ as the unit, a rotation diagonal in the mode basis with weights $s_{j}$ is implemented inside the level by $U(\theta) = e^{\theta J\sum s_{j}n_{j}} = \prod_{j}(1 - n_{j} + n_{j}e^{\theta Js_{j}})$, because each $n_{j}$ is an idempotent commuting with $J$ and the others. Since $n_{j} = \tfrac12(1 - \omega_{j})$ with $\omega_{j} = e_{j}f_{j}$, the turn by $2\pi$ is exactly the product of the plane volume elements of the modes of half-integer weight. It acts as the parity $\Gamma$ on all modes if and only if every weight is half-integer; then every odd element has half-integer spin and every even element, every boson built from pairs, has integer spin, at every size. If one mode has integer weight, that mode is a fermion of integer spin; and pairing a spinor mode with a weight-zero mode in each block gives a hopping element of half-integer spin that commutes across blocks and whose normalised sum climbs the known Holstein-Primakoff ladder, a boson of half-integer spin in the limit. The level's own rotations (the kernel rotors, which fix every mode, and the real rotation of two modes, whose weights are $\pm1$ and whose turn by $2\pi$ is $+1$) give integer spin to everything, so the spinor assignment is an input. For the series' attached free fields it is supplied by locality with a positive norm, which is stored separately.

## lay
In the tower every particle is first a fermion, and bosons appear only as collective pairs. One would like the familiar rule that half-integer spin goes with fermions and whole-number spin with bosons to come out of this construction. The calculation shows exactly how much does. Whether two operators commute or anticommute is built into the algebra and holds exactly at every size. How an operator turns under a rotation is extra information: one has to say how each single mode turns. If every single mode turns like a spinor, picking up a minus sign after a full turn, then every pair, and so every collective boson, comes back to itself, and the rule holds exactly, without any limit. If some mode does not, the rule fails, and it fails for bosons too: a pair made of a spinor mode and a spinless mode builds a boson that picks up a minus sign after a full turn. The tower itself does not decide which way the single modes turn; that input comes from the requirement that fields at separated points do not interfere, which the graph treats elsewhere.

## one-liner
On a tower level with unit $J$, the turn by $2\pi$ of a mode rotation of weights $s_{j}$ is $\prod_{s_{j} \notin \mathbb{Z}}e_{j}f_{j}$, equal to the parity exactly when every mode is a spinor; then all collective pair modes have integer spin and commute, at every $N$; otherwise a spinor mode paired with a spin-0 mode gives a commuting boson of half-integer spin.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors} the $v_{j}, w_{j}$ satisfy $\{v_{i}, w_{j}\} = \delta_{ij}$, $\{v_{i}, v_{j}\} = \{w_{i}, w_{j}\} = 0$, so $n_{j}^{2} = v_{j}(w_{j}v_{j})w_{j} = v_{j}(1 - v_{j}w_{j})w_{j} = n_{j}$, and the $n_{j}$ commute pairwise (each is even and built from one plane). Directly, $n_{j} = \tfrac14(e_{j} + f_{j})(e_{j} - f_{j}) = \tfrac14(e_{j}^{2} - e_{j}f_{j} + f_{j}e_{j} - f_{j}^{2}) = \tfrac12(1 - \omega_{j})$, since $f_{j}e_{j} = -e_{j}f_{j}$. By Theorem \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes}, $\omega_{j}^{2} = 1$, $\omega_{j}$ anticommutes with $e_{j}, f_{j}$, commutes with the generators of the other planes and with $g_{1}, g_{2}$, and the $\omega_{j}$ commute pairwise. $J^{2} = g_{1}g_{2}g_{1}g_{2} = -g_{1}^{2}g_{2}^{2} = -1$; $J^{*} = (g_{2}g_{1})(-1)^{2} = g_{2}g_{1} = -J$; and $J$ commutes with every plane generator, which anticommutes with each of $g_{1}, g_{2}$. Hence $J$ commutes with every element of the algebra of the planes. The adjoint is an antiautomorphism with $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$, $n_{j}^{*} = n_{j}$.

\emph{(i).} The summands $\theta Js_{j}n_{j}$ commute pairwise, so $e^{\theta JL_{s}} = \prod_{j}e^{\theta Js_{j}n_{j}}$. Since $n_{j}$ is an idempotent commuting with $J$, $(\theta Js_{j}n_{j})^{k} = (\theta Js_{j})^{k}n_{j}$ for $k \ge 1$, so $e^{\theta Js_{j}n_{j}} = 1 - n_{j} + n_{j}e^{\theta Js_{j}}$, with $e^{\varphi J} = \cos\varphi + J\sin\varphi$ by Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential} ($J$ is a simple bivector of square $-1$). The group law follows from the exponential form, since all factors commute. Unitarity: $U_{s}(\theta)^{*} = \prod_{j}(1 - n_{j} + n_{j}e^{-\theta Js_{j}}) = U_{s}(-\theta)$ because $J^{*} = -J$ and $J$ commutes with $n_{j}$; so $U_{s}(\theta)^{*}U_{s}(\theta) = 1$. Commutation with $J$ is clear. For the action on modes, $[n_{j}, w_{j}] = v_{j}w_{j}w_{j} - w_{j}v_{j}w_{j} = -(1 - v_{j}w_{j})w_{j} = -w_{j}$ and $[n_{k}, w_{j}] = 0$ for $k \ne j$; so $[L_{s}, w_{j}] = -s_{j}w_{j}$, hence $L_{s}w_{j} = w_{j}(L_{s} - s_{j})$ and $U_{s}(\theta)w_{j} = w_{j}e^{\theta J(L_{s} - s_{j})} = e^{-\theta Js_{j}}w_{j}U_{s}(\theta)$; similarly $[L_{s}, v_{j}] = s_{j}v_{j}$ and $U_{s}(\theta)v_{j}U_{s}(\theta)^{*} = e^{\theta Js_{j}}v_{j}$. At $\theta = 2\pi$, $e^{2\pi Js_{j}} = \cos 2\pi s_{j} = (-1)^{2s_{j}}$, so the factor of plane $j$ is $1$ for integer $s_{j}$ and $1 - 2n_{j} = \omega_{j}$ for half-integer $s_{j}$. This gives the product formula. The script checks the product formula, the group law $U_{s}(\pi)^{2} = U_{s}(2\pi)$, unitarity, commutation with $J$ and the action on $v_{j}, w_{j}$ (with $e^{m\pi Js}$ in $\{\pm1, \pm J\}$) for $N = 1, 2, 3$ and all $5^{N}$ assignments with $s_{j} \in \{-\tfrac12, 0, \tfrac12, 1, \tfrac32\}$.

\emph{(ii).} Let $S$ be the set of half-integer modes, so $U_{s}(2\pi) = \prod_{j \in S}\omega_{j}$. For a mode $j$, $\omega_{k}$ commutes with $v_{j}, w_{j}$ for $k \ne j$ and anticommutes for $k = j$. So $\operatorname{Ad}U_{s}(2\pi)$ negates $v_{j}, w_{j}$ for $j \in S$ and fixes them for $j \notin S$, while $\operatorname{Ad}\Gamma$ negates every mode. The two automorphisms agree on the generators $v_{j}, w_{j}$, hence on the algebra of the planes, exactly when $S$ is every mode; then $U_{s}(2\pi) = \prod_{j}\omega_{j} = \Gamma$. $\operatorname{Ad}\Gamma$ fixes products of an even number of modes and negates products of an odd number, so an element of definite spin has half-integer spin exactly when it is odd. Monomials in the modes of two disjoint sets of planes commute or anticommute according to the product of their parities, since modes of distinct planes anticommute; by linearity two odd elements on disjoint sets anticommute and every other pair commutes. Hopping elements $v_{i}w_{j}$, pairing elements $w_{i}w_{j}$, their sums and the density modes are even, so they have integer spin, and those on disjoint blocks commute, at every $N$. The script checks, for $N = 1, 2, 3$ and all $5^{N}$ assignments, that $\operatorname{Ad}U_{s}(2\pi)$ and $\operatorname{Ad}\Gamma$ agree on every mode exactly for the $3^{N}$ all-half-integer assignments ($39$ in all), that $U(2\pi) = \Gamma$ when every weight is $\tfrac12$, and then that all products of two modes are fixed and all modes negated.

\emph{(iii).} If $s_{j}$ is an integer, $j \notin S$, so $\operatorname{Ad}U_{s}(2\pi)w_{j} = w_{j}$ by (ii), while $w_{j}$ anticommutes with every $v_{k}, w_{k}$, $k \ne j$, by the anticommutation relations. For the blocks, $\operatorname{Ad}U_{s}(2\pi)$ negates $v_{\mathrm{lower},i}$ and fixes $w_{\mathrm{upper},i}$, so it negates $b_{i}$. Elements of distinct blocks are even and supported on disjoint planes, so they commute by (ii). The relation $[B, B^{*}] = N_{b}^{-1}\sum_{i}(n_{\mathrm{lower},i} - n_{\mathrm{upper},i})$ and its value $1 - 2k/N_{b}$ on $(B^{*})^{k}P_{\mathrm{pol}}$, with $(B^{*})^{N_{b}+1}P_{\mathrm{pol}} = 0$, are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(ii), which uses only the anticommutation relations and so holds whatever spin is assigned; $B$, a sum of elements of half-integer spin, has half-integer spin. On vectors $(B^{*})^{k}P_{\mathrm{pol}}$ of bounded $k$ the commutator tends to $1$. The script checks all of this for $N_{b} = 1, 2, 3$, with $P_{\mathrm{pol}} = \prod_{i}n_{\mathrm{lower},i}(1 - n_{\mathrm{upper},i})$ as the polarised vector of the left regular representation.

\emph{(iv).} By the preliminaries $J$ commutes with every plane generator, so $e^{\varphi J}$ commutes with the algebra of the planes and $\operatorname{Ad}e^{\varphi J}$ fixes it. For $L$: $v_{0}w_{1} = \tfrac14(e_{0}e_{1} - e_{0}f_{1} + f_{0}e_{1} - f_{0}f_{1})$ and $v_{1}w_{0} = \tfrac14(e_{1}e_{0} - e_{1}f_{0} + f_{1}e_{0} - f_{1}f_{0})$; using anticommutation of distinct generators the mixed terms cancel and $L = \tfrac12(e_{0}e_{1} - f_{0}f_{1})$. $B_{1} = e_{0}e_{1}$ and $B_{2} = f_{0}f_{1}$ commute (they share no generator and are even) and $B_{1}^{2} = -e_{0}^{2}e_{1}^{2} = -1$, $B_{2}^{2} = -f_{0}^{2}f_{1}^{2} = -1$. From the relations, $[L, w_{0}] = -w_{1}$ and $[L, w_{1}] = w_{0}$, so $[L, w_{0} \pm Jw_{1}] = -w_{1} \pm Jw_{0} = \pm J(w_{0} \pm Jw_{1})$: weights $\pm1$. By Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}, $e^{\pi L} = e^{\pi B_{1}/2}e^{-\pi B_{2}/2} = B_{1}(-B_{2}) = -e_{0}e_{1}f_{0}f_{1} = e_{0}f_{0}e_{1}f_{1} = \omega_{0}\omega_{1}$, which negates $v_{0}, w_{0}, v_{1}, w_{1}$, and $e^{2\pi L} = (\omega_{0}\omega_{1})^{2} = 1$. The script checks each identity.

\emph{Reading.} By (ii) and (iii), spin and statistics agree on the whole algebra (and so for all collective modes) if and only if every $s_{j}$ is half-integer, that is if and only if they agree for the single modes. By (iv) neither the kernel rotors nor the real rotations of modes supply half-integer weights; the assignment $s$ is extra data. That the attached free fields' CAR modes are spinors is the locality result cited in the statement, which is not used in the proof.

check_py:
"""synthesis.ladder-bosons-inherit-spin-statistics-from-the-single-modes: exact checks.

A tower level Cl(N, N+2): kernel generators g1 = gen(0), g2 = gen(1) (square -1), J = g1 g2; plane j has
e_j = gen(2 + 2j) (square +1), f_j = gen(3 + 2j) (square -1), v_j = (e_j + f_j)/2 = a*_j, w_j = (e_j - f_j)/2 = a_j,
n_j = v_j w_j, omega_j = e_j f_j, Gamma = prod_j omega_j. * is the CAR adjoint (reversion, a sign per negative-square
generator). A spin assignment s = (s_j), s_j in (1/2)Z, gives U(m pi) = prod_j (1 - n_j + exp(m pi J s_j) n_j), with
exp(m pi J s) = cos + J sin at a multiple of pi/2 (values 1, J, -1, -J).
(1) n_j = (1 - omega_j)/2; for N = 1, 2, 3 and every s in {-1/2, 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2}^N: U(pi)^2 = U(2 pi), U(pi) unitary
    and commuting with J, U(pi) w_j U(pi)* = exp(-pi J s_j) w_j, U(pi) v_j U(pi)* = exp(pi J s_j) v_j, and
    U(2 pi) = prod of omega_j over the half-integer s_j.
(2) Ad U(2 pi) = Ad Gamma on every mode exactly when every s_j is half-integer (N = 1, 2, 3, all assignments
    above); with all s_j = 1/2, U(2 pi) = Gamma; then every hopping, pairing and density element is 2 pi invariant
    and every mode is negated.
(3) Blocks (lower spin 1/2, upper spin 0), N_b = 1, 2, 3: each hopping element b = v_lower w_upper is negated
    by Ad U(2 pi); hopping elements and adjoints of distinct blocks commute; each upper mode is 2 pi invariant and
    anticommutes with the other modes; on (B*)^k P_pol, sum_i [b_i, b_i*] = N_b - 2k for k = 0..N_b and
    (B*)^(N_b + 1) P_pol = 0.
(4) J commutes with every plane generator (N = 1, 2), so Ad exp(phi J) fixes the transport algebra; the real
    rotation L = v_0 w_1 - v_1 w_0 equals (e_0 e_1 - f_0 f_1)/2, a sum of two commuting bivectors of square -1;
    [L, w_0 +- J w_1] = +-J (w_0 +- J w_1) (weights +-1); exp(pi L) = (e_0 e_1)(-f_0 f_1) = omega_0 omega_1 negates
    both modes and exp(2 pi L) = 1.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import itertools

import GA
from tp_premise import premise


def _sq(N):
    return tuple([-1, -1] + [1, -1] * N)


def _dag(x, sq):
    out = {}
    for b, c in x.items():
        g = len(b)
        s = (-1) ** (g * (g - 1) // 2) * (-1) ** sum(1 for i in b if sq[i] == -1)
        out[b] = c * s
    return {b: c for b, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def _prod(xs, sq):
    r = GA.sc(1)
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return r


def _setup(N):
    sq = _sq(N)
    J = GA.mul(GA.gen(0), GA.gen(1), sq)
    e = [GA.gen(2 + 2 * j) for j in range(N)]
    f = [GA.gen(3 + 2 * j) for j in range(N)]
    v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(e[j], f[j])) for j in range(N)]
    w = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(e[j], f[j])) for j in range(N)]
    n = [GA.mul(v[j], w[j], sq) for j in range(N)]
    om = [GA.mul(e[j], f[j], sq) for j in range(N)]
    return sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om


def _phase(m, s, J):
    t = (2 * m * s) % 4
    return [GA.sc(1), J, GA.sc(-1), GA.neg(J)][int(t)]


def _U(m, spins, n, J, sq):
    return _prod([GA.add(GA.sub(GA.sc(1), nj), GA.mul(_phase(m, s, J), nj, sq)) for s, nj in zip(spins, n)], sq)


def _ad(u, x, sq):
    return GA.mul(GA.mul(u, x, sq), _dag(u, sq), sq)


SPINS = [F(1, 2), F(0), F(-1, 2), F(1), F(3, 2)]


def check_two_pi_rotation_is_the_product_of_half_integer_plane_volumes():
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    premise("tower.volume-elements-planes")
    premise("std-algebra.bivector-exponential")
    ok = True
    for N in (1, 2, 3):
        sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om = _setup(N)
        ok &= all(GA.eq(GA.add(GA.mul(v[i], w[j], sq), GA.mul(w[j], v[i], sq)), GA.sc(1 if i == j else 0))
                  for i in range(N) for j in range(N))
        ok &= all(GA.eq(n[j], GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(GA.sc(1), om[j]))) for j in range(N))
        for spins in itertools.product(SPINS, repeat=N):
            U1 = _U(1, spins, n, J, sq)
            U2 = _U(2, spins, n, J, sq)
            ok &= GA.eq(GA.mul(U1, U1, sq), U2)
            ok &= GA.eq(GA.mul(_dag(U1, sq), U1, sq), GA.sc(1)) and GA.commutes(U1, J, sq)
            ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U1, w[j], sq), GA.mul(_phase(-1, spins[j], J), w[j], sq)) for j in range(N))
            ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U1, v[j], sq), GA.mul(_phase(1, spins[j], J), v[j], sq)) for j in range(N))
            half = [om[j] for j in range(N) if spins[j].denominator == 2]
            ok &= GA.eq(U2, _prod(half, sq))
    return ok


def check_spin_statistics_holds_exactly_when_every_mode_is_half_integer():
    premise("tower.volume-elements-planes")
    ok = True
    count = 0
    for N in (1, 2, 3):
        sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om = _setup(N)
        Gam = _prod(om, sq)
        for spins in itertools.product(SPINS, repeat=N):
            U2 = _U(2, spins, n, J, sq)
            same = all(GA.eq(_ad(U2, x, sq), _ad(Gam, x, sq)) for x in v + w)
            allhalf = all(s.denominator == 2 for s in spins)
            ok &= same == allhalf
            count += 1 if same else 0
        U2 = _U(2, [F(1, 2)] * N, n, J, sq)
        ok &= GA.eq(U2, Gam)
        pairs = [GA.mul(v[i], w[j], sq) for i in range(N) for j in range(N)] + \
                [GA.mul(w[i], w[j], sq) for i in range(N) for j in range(N)]
        ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U2, x, sq), x) for x in pairs)
        ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U2, x, sq), GA.neg(x)) for x in v + w)
    # all-half-integer assignments among the 5 + 25 + 125 tried: 3 + 9 + 27
    return ok and count == 39


def check_half_integer_spin_boson_from_a_spinor_and_a_scalar_mode():
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    premise("synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum")
    ok = True
    for Nb in (1, 2, 3):
        sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om = _setup(2 * Nb)
        spins = [F(1, 2), F(0)] * Nb
        U2 = _U(2, spins, n, J, sq)
        b = [GA.mul(v[2 * i], w[2 * i + 1], sq) for i in range(Nb)]
        ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U2, x, sq), GA.neg(x)) for x in b)
        ok &= all(GA.commutes(b[i], y, sq) for i in range(Nb) for j in range(Nb) if j != i
                  for y in (b[j], _dag(b[j], sq)))
        up = [w[2 * i + 1] for i in range(Nb)]
        ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(U2, x, sq), x) for x in up)
        ok &= all(GA.anticommutes(up[0], y, sq) for y in w[1:] + v[2:])
        Bs = GA.add(*[_dag(x, sq) for x in b])
        Bc = GA.add(*b)
        C = GA.sub(GA.mul(Bc, Bs, sq), GA.mul(Bs, Bc, sq))
        P = _prod([GA.mul(n[2 * i], GA.sub(GA.sc(1), n[2 * i + 1]), sq) for i in range(Nb)], sq)
        x = P
        for k in range(Nb + 1):
            ok &= x != {} and GA.eq(GA.mul(C, x, sq), GA.scal(F(Nb - 2 * k), x))
            x = GA.mul(Bs, x, sq)
        ok &= x == {}
    return ok


def check_rotations_of_the_level_itself_give_integer_spin():
    premise("std-algebra.bivector-exponential")
    ok = True
    for N in (1, 2):
        sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om = _setup(N)
        ok &= GA.eq(GA.mul(J, J, sq), GA.sc(-1))
        ok &= all(GA.commutes(J, GA.gen(i), sq) for i in range(2, 2 + 2 * N))
    sq, J, e, f, v, w, n, om = _setup(2)
    L = GA.sub(GA.mul(v[0], w[1], sq), GA.mul(v[1], w[0], sq))
    B1 = GA.mul(e[0], e[1], sq)
    B2 = GA.mul(f[0], f[1], sq)
    ok &= GA.eq(L, GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(B1, B2)))
    ok &= GA.commutes(B1, B2, sq) and GA.eq(GA.mul(B1, B1, sq), GA.sc(-1)) and GA.eq(GA.mul(B2, B2, sq), GA.sc(-1))
    for sgn in (1, -1):
        y = GA.add(w[0], GA.scal(F(sgn), GA.mul(J, w[1], sq)))
        ok &= GA.eq(GA.sub(GA.mul(L, y, sq), GA.mul(y, L, sq)), GA.scal(F(sgn), GA.mul(J, y, sq)))
    R = GA.mul(B1, GA.neg(B2), sq)          # exp(pi L) = exp(pi B1/2) exp(-pi B2/2)
    ok &= GA.eq(R, GA.mul(om[0], om[1], sq))
    ok &= all(GA.eq(_ad(R, x, sq), GA.neg(x)) for x in w + v)
    ok &= GA.eq(GA.mul(R, R, sq), GA.sc(1))
    return ok
